Weapons.About.DamageType: The kind of damage: AP (armor-piercing), HE, small arms, artillery… Each kind has its own levels and its own effect on each armor.
Weapons.About.Level: The damage's level within its kind. For AP kinds, a higher level beats thicker armor. Only the levels the kind has are taken.
Weapons.About.DamageRadius: Radius around the impact that also takes damage.
Weapons.About.SuppressionRadius: Radius around the impact that also takes suppression.
Weapons.About.SuppressesOnMiss: A near miss still suppresses the target.
Weapons.About.WeakerWithRange: Kinetic AP and AA guns only: the table that lowers their damage level with distance. None for missiles, HEAT and HE.
Weapons.About.Tandem: A tandem warhead, as the game gives the PzF 3, RPG-29, Vikhr and Ataka (17 weapons). Only matters against units with explosive reactive armour: there the shot's damage is changed by the game according to its damage type. Against other units it does nothing.
Weapons.About.HarmlessToAllies: Doesn't damage your own or allied units. On for 343 weapons, mostly guns, machine guns and rifles.
Weapons.About.FireChance: Chance, from 0 to 1, that a shot landing starts the weapon's Fire, multiplied by how flammable the ground there is. Only weapons with a Fire use it: 0.05 to 1 in the game. With Ignores flammability on, every shot landing starts the Fire.
Weapons.About.Fire: The fire an incendiary weapon starts (FireDescriptor.ndf); none for others.
Weapons.About.Smoke: The smoke a smoke round makes (SmokeDescriptor.ndf); none for others.
Weapons.About.TopArmor: Always strikes the target's top armor. On for 41 weapons: bombs and cluster munitions.
Weapons.About.TopArmorOnHit: A hit strikes the top armor. On for artillery, mortars and bombs (282 weapons).
Weapons.About.ArmorFromImpact: The armor side hit is worked out from where the shot lands, not from where it was fired. On for artillery, mortars and bombs.
Weapons.About.IgnoresFlammability: Every shot landing starts the weapon's Fire, whatever the ground, without rolling Fire chance (which must still be above 0). Off: Fire chance is multiplied by how flammable the ground is: dense forest 0.8, light forest 0.6, buildings 0.2, rocks 0.1, open ground and water 0. On for the 21 true incendiaries (napalm, flamethrowers).
Weapons.About.Minimum: Shortest range against ground units: closer targets can't be fired at.
Weapons.About.Helicopters: Longest range against helicopters; 0 if it can't fire at them.
Weapons.About.Planes: Longest range against planes; 0 if it can't fire at them.
Weapons.About.Missiles: Longest range against incoming missiles: the range used when the target is a projectile in flight. Only the two active protection systems have one.
Weapons.About.MissilesMinimum: Shortest range against incoming missiles: the minimum range used when the target is a projectile in flight.
Weapons.About.Stopped: Hit chance per shot when the firing unit is stopped, before range, suppression and other modifiers.
Weapons.About.Moving: Hit chance per shot when the firing unit moves.
Weapons.About.FallsWithDistance: Hit chance rises as the target gets closer: up to 4 times at very close range, no change at full range.
Weapons.About.Critical: Raises the chance that a hit causes a critical effect. 25 on most weapons, 0 on the others.
Weapons.About.DispersionFar: How far a miss lands from the target at maximum range.
Weapons.About.DispersionNear: How far a miss lands from the target at minimum range.
Weapons.About.SpreadAngle: Half-angle of a cone that makes the spread grow with distance: at distance d, d × tan(this angle) is added to the dispersion radius from Disp. near and Disp. far. 0 for guns; above 0 for missiles, bombs and flamethrowers. In WARNO it is in radians and must be from 0 to 0.785 (45°); Steel Division 2 not checked.
Weapons.About.CorrectedSpread: Only for weapons firing artillery shells; leave it at 0 on others. Spread multiplier once fire is corrected on a spot: 0.7 in the game, 0.25 for guided shells.
Weapons.About.SuccessiveHits: 1, 3 or 5 in the game. The most successive hits on the same target that count: each raises the hit chance by 3 % of itself. Changing target, or the target moving more than 7,067 GRU between two shots, starts the count again.
Weapons.About.AccuracyBase: Always 0 in the game. Added to the hit chance in every case, stopped or moving.
Weapons.About.AccuracyTargeted: Always 0 in the game. Not used by the hit, armour-piercing or critical rolls in WARNO; Steel Division 2 not checked.
Weapons.About.Aiming: Seconds from seeing a target to the first shot.
Weapons.About.PerSalvo: Shots in one salvo, before reloading. Weapons sharing an ammo box must keep the same number.
Weapons.About.AtOnce: Shots fired at the same moment within a salvo.
Weapons.About.BetweenShots: Seconds between shots within a salvo. Unused when a salvo is one shot.
Weapons.About.Reload: Seconds between two salvos: the reload time.
Weapons.About.ReloadAtLeast: Shortest reload when it varies: the reload is then a random time between this and Reload, at most, to 0.01 s, instead of Reload. -1 (off): the reload doesn't vary. Set on 46 aircraft rockets.
Weapons.About.ReloadAtMost: Longest reload when it varies: the reload is then a random time between Reload, at least, and this. -1 (off) when it doesn't vary.
Weapons.About.Supply: Supply used to refill one salvo: the game works out the supply per shot as Supply ÷ Per salvo. In WARNO that must be from 0.001 to 1,000; Steel Division 2 not checked.
Weapons.About.ShownPerSalvo: How many rounds each salvo counts as in the ammunition the game shows (at least 1): the count shown is the salvos left times this, and the ammunition gauge is worked out from it. An AA gun firing 6 shots a salvo shows 48.
Weapons.About.EffectsBetween: Seconds between firing effects. A continuous-fire look starts its effects this many seconds apart; an instant-fire look doesn't use it. Shorter than Between shots on fast-firing guns.
Weapons.About.FiresMoving: On: fires while the unit moves. Off: fires only while the unit is stopped.
Weapons.About.MustDeploy: Must stop and deploy before firing, as howitzers do: the weapon is packed up while the unit moves, and fires again only once the unit has stopped and finished deploying. A unit carrying such a weapon needs a TWeaponDeploymentModuleDescriptor (its deploy and pack times), and a unit with that module needs at least one such weapon.
Weapons.About.FirePosition: Offers the Fire Position order: firing at a spot on the ground with no target.
Weapons.About.SalvosAtPosition: Salvos fired by one Fire Position order: the weapon stops firing on the position once it has fired this many. Set exactly on the weapons that offer it.
Weapons.About.Indirect: Fires over obstacles, as artillery does; no for direct fire.
Weapons.About.Reflex: Fires on its own at enemies it sees, without an attack order. Off for artillery, mortars and bombs.
Weapons.About.NoReflexOnPriority: No reflex shots while the unit has a priority target. On for guided missiles (187).
Weapons.About.OnePerDistrict: On for most direct-fire weapons (677). In a town district, only one of the units the shot could hit is hit, picked at random, enemies first.
Weapons.About.ProjectileKind: How the shot travels and lands: shell, artillery shell (whether it hits depends on its spread, and with Submunitions its bomblets are followed in flight), bomb, grenade, or guided missile (launched as a separate missile that flies to the target). Fake has no real projectile.
Weapons.About.Speed: Shells and guided missiles fly straight to the target at this speed, so the flight time is the distance divided by it. Guided missiles build up to it at their Acceleration. 0 for bombs.
Weapons.About.Acceleration: Guided missiles only: how fast the missile gains speed until it reaches Speed. Its flight time is worked out from both.
Weapons.About.Arc: The angle the shot is fired at: with Speed it sets the arc the shot flies. Set on artillery shells and grenades (15° to 60° in the game).
Weapons.About.Corrections: Missiles only: seconds between two corrections of the missile's course.
Weapons.About.FireAndForget: On: once fired, the missile flies on without the unit that fired it. Off: while it flies, the missile checks that the unit that fired it still exists and, for direct fire, still sees the target; when either fails, its flight changes. On for 57 missiles.
Weapons.About.Guidance: Who the missile can fire at. Radar: not at drones (units tagged Non_Radar_Targetable). Anti-radar: only at units carrying a radar-guided weapon. None for the others (32 missiles have one).
Weapons.About.Submunitions: Releases bomblets, as cluster bombs and shells do (38 weapons).
Weapons.About.Missile: The missile flown (MissileDescriptors.ndf); none for other weapons.
Weapons.About.ShotsInOrder: Off for guns, artillery and rockets (570). On: before a salvo, the game sorts where its shots will land across the line of fire (along it, for some shots), so they land in a sweep. Off: they land in the order they were picked.
Weapons.About.AffectedByNumber: On for 252 weapons: machine guns, rifles and autocannons. Each shot's damage is multiplied by how many of the weapon are still in use: its Count (×) times the share of the unit's health left, rounded up, at least 1. A squad that has lost men hits less hard. Off: the Count doesn't multiply the damage. Steel Division 2 not checked.
Weapons.About.Noise: How much firing gives the unit away: 1 to 5 in the game. The unit's firing noise starts at 1, and each shot adds (this − 1) ÷ Shots to full noise, so it reaches this value after that many shots. 1: firing doesn't give the unit away.
Weapons.About.ShotsToNoise: Shots before Firing noise is at its full value: each shot adds (Firing noise − 1) ÷ this.
Weapons.About.Picture: The weapon's picture in the game's interface. The ✎ on the picture above, or a click on this value, picks another weapon's.
Weapons.About.Traits: The trait icons the game shows beside the weapon. Interface only. A click on the value ticks them in a list of the game's traits.
Weapons.About.ComparedWith: The group the weapon is compared within: the game's file of weapon ranges gives each group's lowest and highest values (damage, suppression, ranges, aiming time and so on), which scale the weapon's stat bars.
Weapons.About.ShowsDamage: On: the weapon's damage counts in the damage the game shows for the unit (the highest of its weapons'). Off: it is left out of that figure.
Weapons.About.ShowsSalvoAccuracy: On: the hit chance shown when aiming is the chance that at least one shot of the salvo hits. Off: it shows one shot's chance.
Weapons.About.EffectSize: The power given to the impact effect when the shot lands: medium (2) or ultra heavy (5).
Weapons.About.ImpactEffect: The effect played where the shot lands. It is given the ground type, the shot's direction, the damage and suppression radii, and Effect size.
Weapons.About.Cursor: The cursor shown when the unit aims at a target with this weapon.
